title: Evaluation Criteria
description: How independent labs evaluate and rate vendor products: certification under TCSEC, ITSEC and Common Criteria, followed by management accreditation.

nodes.title: Certification
nodes.description:
Evaluation criteria are independent, objective systems for evaluating products, so you do not have to trust a vendor's own marketing claims.
Certification is the first of the two major steps: a comprehensive technical analysis of a product to make sure it meets your needs. This is where an independent testing lab evaluates the product and gives it a rating.
How it works: the vendor pays an independent lab to evaluate its product against one of the evaluation criteria. The lab tests the product, rates it and writes a report that the vendor hands out to customers. Customers trust the rating because it comes from an independent lab, not the vendor.

children.title: TCSEC (Orange Book)
children.description:
Trusted Computer System Evaluation Criteria: one of the oldest evaluation criteria. Known as the Orange Book because of its orange cover.
It evaluates confidentiality only, for stand-alone systems only, and rates products on seven functional levels.

children.title: Confidentiality only
children.description: TCSEC was designed to evaluate only the confidentiality that a system provides.

children.title: Single Box only
children.description: TCSEC was designed to evaluate only products that are not connected to a network: single, stand-alone boxes.

children.title: Functional Levels
children.description:
TCSEC defines seven functional levels that a product can be rated at. Each level builds on the previous one.
From lowest to highest: D1, C1, C2, B1, B2, B3, A1.

children.title: D1 – failed or not tested
children.description: The lowest possible rating: the product failed the evaluation or was not tested.

children.title: C1 – Weak protection mechanisms
children.description: The product provides weak protection mechanisms.

children.title: C2 – Strict login procedures
children.description:
Adds strict login procedures.
C2 is the most common rating for products.

children.title: B1 - Security labels
children.description: Labeling becomes a requirement at B1. Remember: B1 means labels.

children.title: B2 - Security labels and verification of no covert channels
children.description: Security labels, plus verification that there are no covert channels.

children.title: B3 - Security labels, verification of no covert channels, and must stay secure during start-up
children.description: Security labels and verification of no covert channels, and the product must stay secure during start-up.

children.title: A1 – Verified design
children.description:
The highest possible functional rating: a verified design.
So secure that it is virtually unusable.

children.title: ITSEC
children.description:
Information Technology Security Evaluation Criteria: a big improvement on the older TCSEC.
It evaluates confidentiality and integrity, works for networked devices, uses the same functional levels as TCSEC, and adds assurance levels.

children.title: Confidentiality + Integrity
children.description: ITSEC evaluates not just the confidentiality a product provides, but also its integrity.

children.title: Networked devices
children.description: ITSEC can evaluate devices that are connected to a network.

children.title: Same Functional levels as TCSEC
children.description: ITSEC uses exactly the same functional levels as TCSEC: D1, C1, C2, B1 and so on.

children.title: Assurance Levels
children.description:
The last major improvement: ITSEC evaluates assurance as well as functionality.
- Functionality: what a system should do.
- Assurance: how you verify and test that it is working correctly.
The assurance levels are called evaluation levels, or E levels. There are seven of them, E0 to E6.
You do not need to memorize the specifics of each E level.

children.title: E0
children.description:
The lowest of the seven ITSEC assurance levels (E0 to E6).
You do not need to memorize the specifics of each E level.

children.title: E1
children.description:
One of the seven ITSEC assurance levels, between E0 (lowest) and E6 (highest).
You do not need to memorize the specifics of each E level.

children.title: E2
children.description:
One of the seven ITSEC assurance levels, between E0 (lowest) and E6 (highest).
You do not need to memorize the specifics of each E level.

children.title: E3
children.description:
One of the seven ITSEC assurance levels, between E0 (lowest) and E6 (highest).
You do not need to memorize the specifics of each E level.

children.title: E4
children.description:
One of the seven ITSEC assurance levels, between E0 (lowest) and E6 (highest).
You do not need to memorize the specifics of each E level.

children.title: E5
children.description:
One of the seven ITSEC assurance levels, between E0 (lowest) and E6 (highest).
You do not need to memorize the specifics of each E level.

children.title: E6
children.description:
The highest of the seven ITSEC assurance levels (E0 to E6).
You do not need to memorize the specifics of each E level.

children.title: Common Criteria
children.description:
The Common Criteria for Information Technology Security Evaluation: the latest and greatest evaluation criteria. Everyone just calls it Common Criteria.
The process: define a Protection Profile, identify the Target of Evaluation, the vendor writes a Security Target, the lab tests the functional and assurance requirements, and an EAL is assigned.

children.title: ISO 15408
children.description: Common Criteria has been adopted as an international standard: ISO 15408.

children.title: Protection Profile
children.description: The evaluation process starts with a Protection Profile (PP): the security requirements for a class of security devices, such as firewalls or smart cards.

children.title: Target of Evaluation
children.description:
The Target of Evaluation (TOE): the specific product or system, provided by the vendor, that will be evaluated.
Example: a Cisco ASA 5515-X firewall.

children.title: Security Targets
children.description: The Security Target (ST): a document the vendor prepares that defines the functional and assurance security properties and capabilities the vendor claims are built into the TOE.

children.title: Functional & Assurance Requirements
children.description: The independent testing lab tests the functional and assurance aspects of the TOE.

children.title: Assign EAL
children.description:
The end result of the evaluation is an Evaluation Assurance Level (EAL) rating.
There are seven levels, and they build on each other. Memorize the levels and their order.

children.title: EAL1 – Functionally tested
children.description: The lowest rating: only the functionality of the product was tested.

children.title: EAL2 – Structurally tested
children.description: Only the structure of the product was tested.

children.title: EAL3 – Methodically tested & checked
children.description: The product was methodically tested and checked.

children.title: EAL4 – Methodically designed, tested & reviewed
children.description: The product was methodically designed, tested and reviewed.

children.title: EAL5 – Semi formally designed & tested
children.description: The product was semi-formally designed and tested.

children.title: EAL6 – Semi formally verified designed & tested
children.description: The product's design was semi-formally verified, and the product was tested.

children.title: EAL7 – Formally verified designed and tested
children.description: The best possible rating: the product's design was formally verified, and the product was tested.

nodes.title: Accreditation
nodes.description:
The second major step, and the final step in choosing a product: management's approval and sign-off.
Official management sign-off to buy and deploy a product in the organization, for a set period of time.
The point of evaluation criteria is to help the organization compare products and choose the best solution.
